Is the following linter error expected?

import Std.Tactic.Lint

/-- My foo function. -/
def foo (_ : Nat) := 0

#lint

The underscore makes it clear I want this to be an unused argument.
It is expected, yes. The mathlib/std unused arguments linter looks at the underlying expression and doesn't care about argument names
Is this considered to be a bug or a feature?
a behavior :shrug:
(unlike the core unused-arg linter, which fails to catch non-syntactic uses, right?)
I can see uses for it
right @James Gallicchio
for instance you can use def foo (_ : Nat) : Nat := by assumption to make a non-constant function with an unnamed argument
calling the variable x there would probably trigger the core linter
the mathlib linter is more about actually detecting constant functions

Hmm, should we change this? I think it's a bit odd to have a convention where we can say to one linter "it's okay if this argument is unused" in one manner, but have to say "no, really, it's okay that it's unused" in a different way to another (via nolint) :)

(batteries#1834 if we think _x or _ should disable the unusedArguments linter)

It was very much intentional that the unusedArguments linter flags argument names that start with _, because a main feature of it is that it finds unused typeclass arguments. Those are typically not named, so the syntax linter will (and should) not complain (EDIT: until lean#7956 is implemented). But the environment linter should.

Example:

import Batteries

/-- a definition -/
def foo [Mul Nat] [DecidableEq Type] := 3

/--
info: -- Found 0 errors in 1 declarations (plus 0 automatically generated ones) in the current file with 10 linters


-- All linting checks passed!
-/
#guard_msgs in
#lint

For non-instance arguments, allowing names that start with _ seems reasonable to me (and for instance arguments, explicitly given names starting with _ might also be allowed, but I don't think we can check for that, other than "does this fall outside the automatic naming scheme for instance implicit arguments")

To react to a comment in batteries#1834, it is definitely not intentional that unusedArguments is doesn't run on theorems anymore. That is the point of unusedArguments (in fact, IIRC there were some discussions to disable the linter altogether on definitions, so theorems were always the main point).

cc @Thomas Murrills
(it's unfortunate that the tests from Lean 3 were never ported to Lean 4)
I made a PR with my desired behavior in batteries#1878.

Ooh, I see. Let me PR a fix.

I think the thing we "actually" want to do is erase macro scopes before considering whether we should exempt something, as the _@ from macro scopes is what's providing the false positive.
Oops, race condition :sweat_smile:
The new linter shows some false positives, but I'm not sure what I'm doing wrong yet. If you want to adopt this and close my PR (or push to it directly), please be my guest!
What are the false positives, exactly? (Also maybe I can get away with github suggestions, let's see! :grinning_face_with_smiling_eyes:)

Here is the CI run on batteries:
https://github.com/fpvandoorn/std4/actions/runs/28119773155/job/83268416232
it seems to start flagging used arguments now.
Oh, maybe the problem is its interaction with partial def...

not sure what the value is of a partial def, we probably have to disable the linter for that.
I'm done with Leaning for today. As I said, feel free to push to my PR.
Ok, sounds good!
(Do I have write access?)
Ah, I do not.
I'll make copy of the PR to save you the trouble of giving me write access to your fork :)

Floris van Doorn said:

Oh, maybe the problem is its interaction with partial def...

Ah yeah, indeed the issue was value? with allowOpaque also inspecting the value of opaque definitions, not just theorems.

batteries#1879 (sorry, worked on something else for a while).

I think your approach to special-case instance names was right, we just may as well check the binder info instead of looking for an inst prefix. Normally I would have just made these suggestions of course, but maybe this will let it get merged faster :)
Relevant side issue here: #batteries > Consolidate linters?
